correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=1, the exact ball averages on G_m=K_(m+2) minus uv make the centered nonlinear maximal map the pointwise maximum of finitely many nonnegative row-stochastic selections; operator norm equals the largest singular norm of a selection. The K_N maximizing vector has high singleton and low whole-ball rows, with at least two low vertices; placing deficient u,v among low entries strictly boosts their neighborhood averages, proving ||M_G||_2>||M_K_N||_2. Any extremizer has u,v below the universal-vertex mean, ruling out their singleton rows. Permuting universal rows gives k singleton and m-k whole-ball groups; their normalized group-constant subspace yields the stated <=4x4 T and contrasts have squared eigenvalues <=1. For m=3, independent complete enumeration of 72 matrices gives 69 below 7/5 and exactly three maximizing permutations with largest squared singular value 1.4163423965462847. The exact determinant factorization of the 5x5 representative verifies cubic 400λ³-655λ²+126λ-1. At m=1,2 there is a unique winning unsplit universal-row pattern. The finite enumeration establishes first symmetry-breaking case, not all-m compression, which follows analytically.

value.rationale: A single missing edge is the canonical perturbation of K_n for maximal averaging operators. The theorem proves strict norm sensitivity for every n, transforms exponential row-selection enumeration into O(n) blocks of bounded dimension, and identifies the first broken universal-clique extremizer symmetry with sharp algebraic norm and equality rays. This has intrinsic harmonic-analytic and graph-structural meaning independent of computing a small cubic.
